newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended slightly lower after late losses but the market was trading relatively steady given steeper declines in U.S. Treasuries and Bunds.
The March Swiss Confederate Bond futures contract retested Tuesday's contract high of 121.00, but failed to get above that level. The price crumbled in the last hour of trade.

The City of Zurich issued a 200 million Swiss franc domestic bond. The 10-year offering, with a 3.50 percent coupon was priced at issue at 100.80. It was quoted on screens at 3.52 percent and traded at 3.53 percent, traders said. It was issued about eight basis points above comparable Confederate bonds.
The traded price was seen about 6.5 basis points above Confederate bonds in late activity.
The new issue got off to a strong start. According to one bank in the syndicate, the group included most big Swiss banks, with the exception of SBC Warburg.

Swiss short-term maturities were easier after ending steady on Tuesday. Money market traders said shorter dates were slightly firmer in the morning ahead of the end of the latest bank liquidity period on Thursday, February 20.
March Conf futures down one at 120.75.
March Comi medium-term bond unchanged at 112.00
Mar Euro Swiss francs down two at 98.25.
